data.narrative:
Black Forest Labs, a Series B AI & Software company founded by Robin Rombach, Andreas Blattmann, and Patrick Esser, is evaluated against a comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Palantir, PLTR). The company has raised $300M to date against a stated last post-money valuation of $3.25B, which the analysis flags as unreliable given the implied 20x ratio to total capital deployed.

Stage-progression methodology is inapplicable here; the standard 1.9x Series B step-up produces an implied $6.2B valuation that materially exceeds the sanity threshold relative to capital raised. Peer-median analysis is the applicable triangulation method. Across three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Scale AI ($29.0B), Physical Intelligence ($5.6B), and Field AI ($2.0B)—the median valuation is $5.6B, with a range spanning $2.0B to $29.0B.

The single-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $4.8B to $6.4B, centered on $5.6B. Key uncertainties include the wide dispersion within the peer set (Scale AI trades at a significant premium) and the materiality of relative product maturity, go-to-market traction, and unit economics not captured in stage alone. Any revaluation should hinge on evidence of differentiated revenue scale or capital efficiency relative to the Physical Intelligence and Field AI anchors.
